questions.help:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES
 
2 Lighting systems
The functions of the lights on the vehicle are to see and be seen.
The lighting system allows the driver, in low lighting conditions, to illuminate the roadway in order to view the road and monitor the traffic. In doing so the driver can see any potential hazard in time to react. For this reason, there is a need to frequently check the lighting system so as to ensure compliance with the lighting regulations and operational use. (Lights and bulbs should be checked to ensure they are working correctly. Make sure that the lights are not dirty or broken, etc.)
The duration of the bulbs (both conventional and halogen) depends on the evaporation of the filament. That’s why it is recommended, that if one needs replacing, the other one should be changed, too.
(Página 62 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions      
     
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided  
2.3 The key: Reducing the risk
It is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.
In many collisions, the driver claims that the vehicle or road was an associated or main factor but the simple truth is that the driver could have behaved in a different way that would have avoided a collision. For example, if the driver had realised that the tyres were defective (by maintenance and inspection) they could have avoided the puncture (blow out) or if they had adopted an adequate speed and a safe distance when driving in the rain or snow, they could have avoided running into the vehicle ahead of them.
Proper maintenance and responsible driving reduces the chances that a “vehicle factor” or a “road factor” will be a cause of a collision.
(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
¿Qué efectos tiene en la conducción una conversación por el móvil que supere el minuto y medio?

questions.help:
DISTRACTIONS    
   
8.1 Circumstances of collisions due to phone use
Research indicates that there are four moments especially dangerous when using a mobile phone whilst driving:
Whilst speaking. Even with a hand free set, the first minute and a half of the conversation requires a high degree of focus and attention. After this time the driver fails to receive 40% of road signals and information and their average speed is reduced by 12% however they also take longer to react to a hazard or event.
When terminating a call. The effect is worsened when the driver continues to think about the conversation. Normally, it takes some time for the driver’ concentration to return fully to driving and monitoring the traffic and environment.
(Página 36 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
9 Airbags

In the event of a collision, unless the seat belt is fastened, (buckled) there is a high risk that the head will hit the airbag when it is still inflating and, because of the force exerted in this inflation process, serious injuries can occur, which can even be fatal.

10.1 Head restraints – correct usage
To ensure optimum safety, the top of the restraint must be at the same height as the top of the head. There must be very little distance between the head and the restraint: it should be as close as possible, bearing in mind the need to maintain freedom of movement of the head and comfort (approximately 4 cm’s is advised).
If the head restraint is adjusted below the nape of neck there is the increased risk of suffering cervical vertebrate (spinal)/neck injury.
(Página 81 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Cuando un conductor da positivo en las pruebas de alcoholemia, ¿los agentes pueden inmovilizar su vehículo?
When a driver gives a positive result in a breathalyser test, may police officers immobilise his vehicle?
questions.help:
ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS
 
18.3 Immobilisation of the vehicle
If the result of tests for alcohol or drugs were positive, the official (police officer) also has the power to prevent the vehicle from continuing any further. They also may detain the vehicle where the driver has refused to carry out such tests. As soon as the driver is fit to drive or another person is able to drive the vehicle on the driver’s behalf the detention ceases to have effect and the vehicle is eligible to continue.
(Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Un permiso de conducción caducado, ¿autoriza a su titular a conducir?
Does an expired driver’s license authorise the holder to drive?
questions.help:
2 Driver documentation
 
2.6 Driving licences - conditions of use/validity
The authority granted by the issuing of a driving licence to drive, is subject to certain conditions and periods of validity.
It is also dependent on the condition that its holder has not completely lost his initial allotment of points.
The normal period of validity may be reduced if, during the time that it remains in force it becomes evident that the holder is suffering from a medical condition, that is susceptible to a worsening of the condition and to a further deterioration of the drivers health.
An expired driving license or permit does not authorise their holders to drive. Using an expired permit or license will give rise to its immediate confiscation.
(Página 23 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
¿Qué le puede suceder a un conductor que circula a velocidad inadecuada?

questions.help:
1 Speed  
 
1.2 Is it dangerous to speed?
Speed by itself does not necessarily constitute a risk factor. However, driving at a high speed makes it difficult for the driver to control the vehicle in a situation should the need arise.
Studies have found that excessive or inappropriate speed is a contributory factor in at least one in four traffic collisions, making it one of the main causes of a traffic collision.
(Página 170 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Un conductor novel, ¿puede sentirse fatigado más fácilmente?
Can a new driver feel fatigued more easily?
questions.help:
FACTORS THAT AFFECT PHYSICAL CAPABILITIES  
 
10.1 Circumstances that cause fatigue
10.1.3 Driver circumstances
Changes of normal driving habits. Most people only drive for short distances and during the day. Therefore special care must be taken when driving long distances (for example, during holidays) and especially when driving at night.
Being a novice driver as this entails not having acquired all of the automated processes involved in driving, and therefore more concentration is required.
Adopting an inappropriate driving posture and position in the seat. This can result in pain, stiffness or muscular overload at the end of the journey.
(Página 37 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:

3.1 Registration certificate
In any event, a new vehicle registration certificate will be issued if the variation in the data communicated affects those shown on the aforementioned document.
In other cases, the owner, as shown on the document, must notify the Traffic Headquarters, within a period of 10 days, (from the date of any transaction) when the vehicle is sold / ownership transferred and provide them with the name and address of the new owner / buyer (acquirer).
The purchaser, new owner, must obtain, within thirty days of the acquisition of the vehicle, a new registration document.
The vehicle cannot be used until this document has been obtained.
(Página 25 del manual 'Learning to drive')
